💡 Travel tips

Entry

Hong Kong passports are visa-free and K-ETA-exempt until 31 Dec 2026, so there's nothing to apply for. Other passports: check K-ETA before you fly. But you still need the free e-Arrival card: anyone without a K-ETA submits it online within 3 days before arrival, so between Nov 12 and 14. Each person does their own, using the official Korean immigration site. Avoid paid "agent" sites.

Getting around

Use Naver Map or KakaoMap (Google Maps is patchy for transit and walking). WOWPASS has T-money built in, so it pays for subways and buses (top up the transit balance at station machines or convenience stores). Otherwise get a T-money card at any GS25, CU or 7-Eleven. For taxis use Kakao T, which takes foreign cards. Every place on this page has a copy button for its Korean name. Paste it into the map app, or show it to the driver.

Airport ↔ Conrad

Taxi ~50–60 min, the airport limousine bus to Yeouido, or AREX to Gongdeok and then a short taxi. Both flights use ICN Terminal 1. On Tue, leave the Conrad by ~18:00 for the 21:50 flight.

Money & tax refund

Cards are accepted nearly everywhere, even small shops. Where they aren't (market stalls, some old-school restaurants), pay with WOWPASS. Top it up with HKD at WOWPASS machines in the airport, many hotels and some subway stations, and you can withdraw any leftover balance as won before you leave. Tax refund: spend ₩15,000+ in one store, show your passport and get the refund instantly at the till (up to ₩1M per purchase). It works at The Hyundai, Olive Young and most shops with a "Tax Free" sign. No tipping in Korea.

Food & queues

Famous spots (Golden Pig, Tosokchon, Sinsajeon) queue. Arrive early, or sign up on the kiosk or CatchTable app and wander until they text you. Many restaurants close on certain days, so check Naver first. Water is free; banchan refills are free.

Handy apps

Naver Map · Kakao T (taxis) · Papago (translation, including the camera for menus) · CatchTable (queues/bookings) · your eSIM app.

Emergency

Tourist helpline 1330 (English, 24h) · Police 112 · Ambulance / fire 119

Entry: e-Arrival card guide, VisitKorea · Tax refund: Korea Navigate · HYROX gear rules: Hyrox Vault

Sat 14 Nov👤 Leona only

Palace → Bukchon → Seochon

Arrival day. Land at 11:40, drop bags, then an afternoon of shops on both sides of the palace and dinner with a friend in Seochon. Keep the pace easy: race tomorrow!
Everyone else: rest day 😴 Sleep in, eat well, maybe a short shake-out jog along the Han River by the Conrad, and get your race bag ready. We all meet up again for HYROX on Sunday.

  1. 11:40

    ✈Land at ICN T1 → Conrad

    Immigration and bags take ~45–60 min. Then a taxi (~60 min) or the airport limousine bus to Yeouido. Drop bags at the Conrad (check-in is usually 15:00) and grab lunch on the way. Tongin Market's lunch café will be closed by the time you reach Seochon.

  2. 14:45

    1Bukchon / Samcheong shop cluster

    ~25 min taxi from the Conrad. Four shops a few minutes apart between Anguk station and the palace's east side. Budget ~1h.

    No reliable public rating founddesign objectssouvenirs

    A Seoul design brand that revives everyday Korean objects: matchboxes, incense, envelopes, colour-reference cards. The Bukchon shop is calm, all wood and plants, near hanok rooftops. A perfect place for small, meaningful gifts.

    What visitors say

    • Heritage-inspired stationery, embroidered goods and cultural candles make great souvenirs.
    • Cosy hanok-view atmosphere. Small, so it's a 20–30 min browse.
    • Fun extra: they can work out a Korean name for you from your birth date.
    Hours
    Daily 11:00–19:30

    3Gopchang jeongol at Yangmani

    ★★★★★ 5.0 DiningCodeHanwoo gopchang jeongol ₩27,000open Sundays

    A Yeouido favourite for Hanwoo (Korean beef) gopchang jeongol: a spicy, rich hotpot loaded with tripe and intestine. They also grill premium tripe and daechang, and the cheese yang-bap fried rice is the finisher. Closest strong pick to the Conrad, and open daily. Many Yeouido office-area spots close on Sundays.

    What visitors say

    • Generous portions of tripe and intestine in the hotpot.
    • Clean, well-made banchan, and lots of lunch options.
    • Bookable, and parking is available.
    Hours

  1. 09:50

    1Golden Pig: join the list, eat ~12:30

    ★★★★☆ 4.3 Google · ~2,970 reviewsMichelin Bib Gourmandwalk-in only

    Seoul's most famous pork BBQ. Thick-cut premium pork belly and neck, grilled for you over clean charcoal with Maldon salt. Finish with kimchi jjigae. No reservations: sign up at the entrance kiosk from ~10:00 with a phone number (a Korean eSIM helps), and they text you when it's your turn.

    What visitors say

    • The pork belly and the service are fantastic. Most say it's worth the price.
    • Lively, but smoky and hot inside. Don't wear your nicest coat.
    • The wait is the hard part: often 2+ hours even on weekdays.
    Hours
    Opens 11:30 (closing time varies by source)
    Where
    149 Dasan-ro, Jung-gu · Yaksu stn (Lines 3/6)
    금돼지식당Naver MapGoogle Maps
    Info: Wanderlog, Dari Korea · photos Tiny Urban Kitchen
  2. 14:00

    2Point of View saved

    Start here: it's the big one.

    ★★★★☆ 4.4 Google via Wanderlog · 224 reviewsstationery3 floors

    A dreamy three-storey stationery shop, one of Asia's best. Floor 1, Tool, has clips in science beakers and playful desk gear. Floor 2, Scene, has objects for everyday life. The top floor, Archive, is a quiet library of beautiful notebooks. ~15 min by taxi from Yaksu.

    What visitors say

    • Every floor is styled like a little museum, which makes it very photogenic.
    • Ranges from everyday pens to high-end collectibles. Easy to overspend!
    • Seongsu all around is great for cafés and pop-ups if you have spare time.
    Hours
    12:00–20:00 · closed the last Monday of each month (that's Nov 30, so you're fine)
    Where
    18 Yeonmujang-gil, Seongdong-gu · Seongsu stn (Line 2)
    포인트오브뷰 성수Naver MapGoogle Maps

  3. 15:30

    3Seongsu shop crawl

    Seongsu's shops are spread across a grid of old factories and warehouses. Wander between these and drop into any pop-up with a queue. They change every few weeks.

    Closed on Nov 16: Monami Store (closed 3rd Mondays, and the 16th is one) and Object Seongsu (closed Mondays). You'll get Object at its Samcheong branch on Saturday. Want the make-your-own pen? Monami opens 10:00 on other days.

    Kasina · Haus Nowhere 👬 fun for the guys

    Kasina is Seoul's go-to sneaker and streetwear shop. Haus Nowhere is Gentle Monster's art-installation flagship. Its installations rotate about every 25 days.

    하우스 노웨어 서울Naver MapGoogle Maps
    카시나 성수Naver MapGoogle Maps

    Beaker · Musinsa Empty

    Beaker is a curated Korean and international fashion and lifestyle store. Musinsa Empty is a rotating pop-up and brand showcase from Korea's biggest fashion platform, so there's always something new.

  4. 18:30

    4DOB Gamjatang saved

    One stop on Line 2 from Seongsu to Konkuk Univ. Then ~40 min back to the Conrad.

    No reliable public rating foundpork-bone stewsolo portions OKopen till 7am

    A Kondae Rodeo Street institution for gamjatang (spicy pork-bone and potato stew) with a soy-based broth simmered with 17 Korean herbs, plus rice cakes and glass noodles. Single lunch portions are available. Finish with fried rice or ramyeon in the leftover broth. There's also a seafood pork-bone jjim, and a mild version for anyone who doesn't do spice.

    What visitors say

    • A deep, herbal, slightly sweet-spicy broth that's different from standard gamjatang.
    • The fried rice at the end is non-negotiable.
    • Open almost 24h, so it's a classic late-night spot near Konkuk Univ.
    Hours
    11:00–07:00 next day, open year-round
    Where
    9-22 Hwayang-dong, Gwangjin-gu · Konkuk Univ stn (Lines 2/7) exit 1
    돕감자탕 건대Naver MapGoogle Maps
    Info + photos: K-Plaza
Plan B: if the Golden Pig list is huge, keep your spot and head to Point of View first (it opens at 12:00). You'll get a text when your table is close, and it's ~15 min back by taxi.

  1. 10:30

    1Sinsajeon brunch 🍯 saved

    Opens at 10:30, so you beat the queue. Honeycomb makgeolli to toast the race. It's 5 o'clock somewhere.

    ★★★★☆ 4.0 Google · 537 reviewsjeon ₩12–20kmakgeolli ₩6–9kopen till 1am

    A buzzy jeon (Korean pancake) pub near Sinsa station, famous for honeycomb makgeolli, rice wine served with a chunk of real honeycomb. Order a mixed jeon platter and celebrate the race. ~25 min by taxi from the Conrad.

    What visitors say

    • The honeycomb makgeolli is the must-try, and almost every table orders it.
    • Crispy jeon pairs perfectly with it. A fun, lively room.
    • Mixed reviews: some call it overrated or touristy. Expect a queue at peak times.
    Hours
